findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl in threat model "login service": extend the model description to include GET /admin/export and add a threat block for the unauthenticated bulk export using ref = "T-DATA-004". Add a control under that threat using ref = "C-AUTHZ-003" with implemented = false until authentication and administrative authorisation are enforced. The new route is registered without requireSession at internal/httpapi/routes.go:10 and streams every user at internal/httpapi/export.go:15-16.

evidence.note: Registers the new GET /admin/export route directly, unlike GET /profile, which is wrapped in requireSession.
Iterates over every row returned by store.Users().
Writes each user's ID, email, and creation timestamp to the response.

model_excerpt.quote: Login service exposing POST /login and GET /profile

relevance.justification: The change adds an administrative bulk-data endpoint outside the modeled routes and exposes personal data without the session validation used by the existing protected route.

findings.suggested_fix: Model GET /admin/export with threat ref T-DATA-004 and control ref C-AUTHZ-003, marked unimplemented while the route lacks authentication and authorisation.
findings.title: Unauthenticated bulk user export is absent from the model

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl in threat model "login service": add an information_asset block for user profile/export data covering user IDs, email addresses, and account creation timestamps, with an appropriate Confidential or Restricted classification. This is required because internal/httpapi/export.go:14-16 introduces these fields in a CSV API response while the existing "user credentials" asset only covers usernames and password hashes.

evidence.note: Defines CSV response fields id, email, and created_at.
Exports these fields for every user in the store.
Emits personal account data in the HTTP response.
Makes the export reachable without the requireSession wrapper used for GET /profile.

model_excerpt.quote: Usernames and password hashes in the users table

relevance.justification: The only modeled information asset covers credentials, while the new unauthenticated response exposes a distinct set of personal account data.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a classified information asset for exported user profile data, including IDs, email addresses, and account creation timestamps.
findings.title: Exported personal account data is not classified

report.summary: Two action-required drift findings: the highest-priority issue is the new unmodeled GET /admin/export endpoint exposing bulk personal data without authentication or authorisation.
